change: Exact b292 five-crate native PGO: add ax_sync to the four-crate root-exporter training and profile-use scopes, with a pre-MMU counter static gate and same 816MHz training workload
hypothesis: Profiling ax_sync in addition to ax_sched/ax_task/ax_runtime/starry_kernel may improve the futex wake/park path without instrumenting broad early-boot dependencies
difference: Single additional hot-path crate relative to boot-valid four-crate profile, same source and workload; broad 213-crate scope has been rejected, and the exact-ELF early-counter gate precedes board use
effect: Current b292 root-only exporter five-crate ax_sync+ax_task+ax_sched+ax_runtime+starry_kernel PGO trained on Plus-1 with 18170 IR records and 790272 counter bytes; uninstrumented profile-use ELF had no __llvm_prf sections and only the known ax_runtime::run_idle partial-profile warning. Two independent valid full20 boots each had 20/20 rows, 380000/380000 samples and zero not_parked. Two-boot p50 median reached Linux RT 90% on 11/20 rows, one more than four-crate resume876, but worst OTHER thread_futex_same_cpu stayed at 14583ns, RT/candidate 57.999%. Same-source ordinary tail gate and third candidate boot not proven.
decision: Reject as final candidate: far below 20/20 90%, and no complete p50/p99/p99.9 regression proof. Preserve training profile, images by SHA, raw two-boot logs, offline comparison and exact wrapper scope; do not promote to production build or request PR merge.
